name: gource
why: Turns a repository's history into an animated tree of contributors, a striking visualisation of version control.

brief.what_it_is: Gource is a command-line visualisation tool that turns a version-controlled project's history into an animated tree. The project's root directory sits at the centre, directories are branches, files are leaves, and contributors appear on the tree at the times they made changes. It reads history from Git, Mercurial, Bazaar and SVN directly, and can also parse logs from several third-party tools for CVS repositories. Running plain `gource` inside a repository shows its log. Output is an on-screen animation, and the homepage notes that video output can be piped to ffmpeg.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage presents Gource as a way to see how a software project grew and who worked on which parts, over time, as an animation rather than a list of commits. The author also says they take paid work for bespoke visualisation and that donations support the open-source project.
brief.how_it_works: Gource generates or reads a log of commits (built in for Git, Mercurial, Bazaar and SVN, or from third-party tool output for CVS), then replays that log as an animated directory tree. Each contributor is drawn working on the tree at the timestamp of their commit. The homepage changelog mentions options such as --start-date, --stop-date, --output-stream and --file-idle-time, which control the date range, output and file display.

commands_seen.context: Run in the current path to view the log of the repository (Git, SVN, Mercurial and Bazaar) in that directory. This is the synopsis command given on the homepage.

brief.install_notes: The homepage lists downloads: a Windows setup exe and zip (both for 0.53 only), and a source tarball gource-0.56.tar.gz for the current release. Building from source needs Boost (0.56 requires 1.69 or later; 0.56 dropped linking boost system), SDL 2 (required since 0.47, SDL 1.2 is no longer supported), GLM (the 0.48 notes say GLM 0.9.8 is safe), and PCRE2 (since 0.52). Font selection can be enabled at configure time with --enable-font-file (0.50). No accounts or runtime services are needed. The Homebrew formula's first-run steps were not confirmed on the homepage.
brief.standout: It turns years of commit history into a moving picture of a project's tree and its contributors, which most version-control tools show only as text. The homepage also has a long, dated changelog going back to 2014, and it points to Logstalgia as a related tool for web-server logs.
brief.status: Maintained, but slow-moving. The latest release is 0.56, dated 6 March 2026, following 0.55 (18 June 2024) and 0.54 (19 January 2023). The homepage's news section is current, but I did not check the repository's commit activity.
brief.caveats: The homepage only lists Windows binaries for 0.53, so Windows users may need to build from source or find a newer build elsewhere. Wayland support is described as experimental (0.54). The homepage does not state a licence, and the Controls wiki and README were linked from the homepage but not fetched. The homepage mentions a man page and README for full options, but I did not read them, so options beyond the ones named in the changelog are unverified. The Homebrew formula does not show any caveats.
quotes: Software projects are displayed by Gource as an animated tree with the root directory of the project at its centre.
Developers can be seen working on the tree at the times they contributed to the project.
For more options and examples see the Controls wiki page, consult the included README file or man page documentation.
fetch_log: https://gource.io/ — fetched OK; returned the homepage text with intro, synopsis, download list and changelog. Not a GitHub repo, so no README was fetched. Did not follow the Controls wiki or man page links.
